items.description: Lifecycle wording ambiguously implies that relationship-only mutations must update updated_at.
items.evidence: Local review and https://github.com/deeprave/specle/pull/42#discussion_r4666317433 identify the missing timestamp update; the current lifecycle policy says every active-record mutation writes updated_at.
items.analysis: The intended semantics, already decided in local review, are that updated_at records lifecycle-status transitions rather than relationship metadata changes.
items.recommendation: Clarify the lifecycle policy wording; do not change relationship mutation code to update updated_at.
items.rationale: User decision: retain status-change-only timestamp semantics and remove the contradictory broader policy wording.

items.description: Relationship mutation replaces whole status records captured before the mutation.
items.analysis: Concurrent lifecycle operations are out of scope, but a state update should not write a cached complete status document. It should reread the durable record immediately before mutation, change only the relationship field, and save that current record.
items.recommendation: Refactor state-related updates to operate on a freshly read status document and mutate only their precise fields; do not add locking or concurrent-update machinery.
items.rationale: User decision: concurrent updates are out of scope, but avoiding stale whole-document writes is required correctness for all state-related updates.

items.description: A symlinked active record could make a relationship mutation write outside the checkout.
items.analysis: This requires a deliberately symlinked internal change directory. Specle does not need to defend ordinary lifecycle work from a user intentionally sabotaging their own checkout.
items.rationale: User decision: fanciful, adversarial scenario outside realistic operating conditions.

items.description: An interruption between replacing two status files can leave a one-sided relationship.
items.analysis: Sudden termination between ordinary file writes is plausible but unlikely. A durable transaction and restart-recovery protocol is disproportionate for this local workflow.
items.recommendation: Reuse the accepted fresh read–modify–write correction; do not add crash-recovery state.
items.rationale: User decision: no additional complexity beyond the state-update approach already accepted for relationship writes.

items.description: A sidecar could be manually linked to more than one parent.
items.analysis: A linked sidecar is delivered with its selected parent and is not a reusable active work item for another parent. The proposed case requires disregarding that lifecycle model.
items.rationale: User decision: once linked, a sidecar is delivered with its parent and will not remain available when another parent becomes active.

items.description: A committed sidecar could have delivery evidence different from its parent.
items.analysis: A with-related-change sidecar is committed only by its parent-owned joint delivery operation, which writes identical delivery evidence to all included members. Independently delivered work must not retain that relationship.
items.rationale: User decision: the proposed mismatch violates the delivery contract rather than exposing a realistic supported state.

items.description: Discovery accepts a reciprocal relationship whose type is not origin.
items.analysis: The supported writer emits origin correctly, but discovery should enforce the relationship role it relies on.
items.recommendation: Require type: origin in the reciprocal-link predicate and add one malformed-link regression test.
items.rationale: User decision: small, contained semantic validation of the reciprocal contract.

items.description: A sidecar could change after delivery discovery but before delivery is recorded.
items.analysis: The proposed race needs another agent, process, or direct edit between a single sequential commit operation's discovery and delivery record.
items.rationale: User decision: concurrent lifecycle updates are unsupported; do not add serialization or versioning.

items.description: Discovery does not independently reject a sidecar name involved in duplicate inventory state.
items.analysis: Global runtime validation already detects duplicate durable identities before ordinary lifecycle operations proceed, as observed in the fix-approved-review-validation reconciliation.
items.rationale: User decision: repeat duplicate-name validation would be redundant.

items.description: Workflow guidance does not direct agents to call the Python relationship helper.
items.analysis: The helper is not an agent-accessible workflow API. Skills can define the durable outcome but cannot prescribe a direct helper call that an agent has no supported mechanism to make.
items.rationale: User decision: direct Python API invocation is unavailable to the agent workflow.

items.description: Completion guidance can be read as recording completion-PR evidence only on the archived parent.
items.analysis: Joint archival is parent-owned, but each archived sidecar remains an independently durable record whose completion history should be self-contained.
items.recommendation: State explicitly that completion reference and event are written to every jointly archived linked record.
items.rationale: User decision: completion applies to all linked changes.

items.description: Replacement status files can lose special shared-worktree permissions.
items.analysis: Specle has no shared-checkout or multi-user permission model; ordinary Git worktrees are user-owned.
items.rationale: User decision: preserving shared-worktree modes is outside the supported operating model.

items.description: Runtime validation does not report malformed or missing reciprocal concurrent relationships.
items.analysis: Global validation should enforce the structural reciprocal contract wherever a concurrent relationship exists. Delivery discovery remains responsible for targeted readiness and delivery-state checks.
items.recommendation: Add structural reciprocal-relationship diagnostics to runtime validation without duplicating delivery eligibility validation.
items.rationale: User decision: validate reciprocal relationships where they exist, while avoiding duplicate targeted validation.

items.description: The schema test accepts delivery without proving that the schema declares or constrains it.
items.analysis: The production schema already declares the field, but additional properties mean the existing positive test would still pass if that declaration were removed.
items.recommendation: Add a discriminating invalid-value or declaration regression test for relationships[].delivery.
items.rationale: User decision: focused test coverage for the existing schema contract.
